purpose: Turn the Pass-3 government/power skeleton into a working governance model — democratic, competent, transparent — so neither the state nor concentrated private wealth becomes the dominant power.
one_sentence: Political power circulates back to the people the way economic surplus circulates through households and communities — under hard rights, competent administration, open public finance, and continuous measurement that interrupt capture.
governing_question: What government architecture allows Constitutional Capitalism to function democratically, competently and transparently without government itself—or concentrated private wealth—becoming the dominant power?
harvest_rule: Integrate Pass-3 GP bones and existing democracy, federalism, justice, transparency, popular sovereignty, government capacity, and related frameworks — no constitutional-law research campaign. Adjudication deferred to Stage 4.

countable_discipline.rule: No COUNTABLE fiscal claims; no invented constitutional holdings

measurement_rule: Count only modules newly crossing FIRST_PASS against the canonical 50-module inventory. Never award progress for rewrite alone.

power_circulation_principle.statement: Political power should circulate back to the people just as economic surplus should circulate back through households and communities.

power_loop.name: Legitimate Power Loop (working)
power_loop.one_sentence: People authorize constrained government through constitution and democratic channels; administration deploys public resources; measured outcomes feed accountability back to people.
power_loop.note: Every arrow now has a GO module mechanism at first-pass depth.

capture_loop.name: Extractive Capture Loop
capture_loop.one_sentence: Concentrated wealth purchases political influence that rewrites rules, contracts, and public-asset claims to enlarge itself.

categories.label: Competition
categories.interrupts: Monopoly of office, contracts, and markets

categories.label: Distributed political power
categories.interrupts: Single-chokepoint capture of elections or institutions

categories.label: Citizen review / recourse
categories.interrupts: No appeal from administrative or automated harm

categories.label: Constitutional rights
categories.interrupts: Majority or agency erasure of liberty floors

capture_circuit_breakers.rule: Categories — not a 30-policy list. Place breakers across Capture Loop arrows.

roles.label: Rulemaker
roles.meaning: Establishes the rules under which people and markets interact.

roles.label: Provider
roles.meaning: Provides genuine public goods/services where appropriate.

roles.label: Investor / Owner
roles.meaning: May hold productive assets where the system specifically justifies public ownership.

roles.label: Referee
roles.meaning: Enforces rights, contracts, competition, and rules.

government_roles.conflict_rule: Roles should not be casually blended. Public ownership of a competitor while regulating rivals is a structural conflict for Stage 3 examination.

public_dollar_accountability_chain.note: Eventually connects directly to Arkansas Budget X-Ray.

operating_questions: Does the expenditure develop Arkansas capability?
Does procurement increase competition or concentration?
Does it create future productive capacity?
procurement_as_economic_flow.guardrail: Local retention cannot become disguised political favoritism. Competition, price, quality, constitutional constraints, and anti-corruption safeguards stay in the architecture.

ai_government_principle.statement: AI may assist government. It should not silently become government.

four_engine_integration.cycle: People grant authority → Government establishes rules/institutions → Human & Community Capability → Production / Ownership / Money Engine → Household Prosperity → Economic power distributed rather than concentrated → Citizens retain meaningful political independence → People hold government accountable → Authority returns to the people
four_engine_integration.antithesis: Economic concentration → political capture → preferential rules → greater economic concentration

contradictions.note: No natural resolution this pass. CX-M21-01 and CX-M21-02 remain Stage 4.

coverage_reconciliation.note: 10 GO modules remapped at 15-field depth; net FIRST_PASS +8 because GO-02 and GO-10 were already counted.

modules.name: Constitutional Order & Rights
modules.now: Arkansas and U.S. constitutional orders exist; rights floors and delegated-authority clarity are unevenly understood as operating constraints on prosperity architecture.
modules.problem: Without hard limits, majorities or agencies can erase liberty; without affirmative structure, government cannot protect households from private capture either.
modules.future_state: Popular sovereignty, protected individual rights, enumerated/delegated authority, due process, equal protection, separation of powers, and explicit boundaries government cannot cross — all operational in the Power Loop start.
modules.mechanism: Harvest constitutional defense, foundational axioms, equal standing, and citizenship frameworks as the rights floor for every later GO module; adjudication of contested holdings deferred to Stage 4.
modules.money_flow: Rights enforcement is core public duty spending; rights themselves are not state assets to monetize.
modules.ownership: People retain rights; government holds limited delegated authority — not ownership of persons or conscience.
modules.household_effect: Security of person, conscience, speech, due process, and equal standing while building surplus and ownership.
modules.government_role: Rulemaker and Referee of the constitutional floor; Provider of enforcement capacity — not Investor/Owner of rights.
modules.market_role: Markets operate inside rights floors; private power cannot buy exemption from equal protection/due process.
modules.transition: Clarify operating constraints before rewriting constitutional text packages.
modules.risks: Constitutional-law research sprawl; rights theater without enforcement capacity.
modules.measurement: Rights-violation remedies available; due-process timelines; equal-standing proxies.
modules.deferred_validation: Arkansas amendment sequencing; federal supremacy conflicts — Stage 4

modules.name: Representative Democracy & Elections
modules.now: Elections authorize offices; districting, ballot access, administration quality, and donor skew can drift representation from consent.
modules.future_state: Representation, election administration, districts, ballot access, and electoral accountability translate public consent into legitimate authority.
modules.problem: If offices become donor assets or uncompetitive monopolies, the Power Loop authorization channel fails.
modules.mechanism: Harvest democracy framework: integrity, access, competitive representation design, civic capacity; age-16 local suffrage remains hypothesis only.
modules.money_flow: Elections are public infrastructure; campaign money must not purchase offices (joins GO-08).
modules.ownership: Offices are public trusts, not private assets.
modules.household_effect: Votes map to policies affecting wages, services, taxes, and place.
modules.government_role: Provider of election infrastructure; Rulemaker of electoral process; Referee of integrity — not partisan owner of outcomes.
modules.market_role: Campaign markets exist under anti-capture rules; election vendors compete under open contracting.
modules.transition: Strengthen administration and access before speculative system swaps.
modules.risks: Partisan capture of election boards; access barriers; donor lock-in.
modules.measurement: Turnout/access metrics; competitiveness proxies; trust panels; residual donor-skew indicators.
modules.evidence_status: WORKING — remapped FIRST_PASS depth from prior substance
modules.deferred_validation: Districting/primary package; age-16 HYP path — Stage 4 / known detail

modules.name: Direct Democracy & Citizen Sovereignty
modules.now: Initiative/referendum and civic channels exist unevenly; capture of elected institutions can leave citizens without independent power.
modules.problem: All power in elected bodies means capture of those bodies captures the people; unbound direct tools can strip rights.
modules.future_state: Initiative, referendum, and related mechanisms keep meaningful citizen power independent of elected institutions — inside GO-01 rights floors.
modules.mechanism: Harvest People's Branch, popular sovereignty, citizen service, and collaborative review channels; process design against petition-industry capture.
modules.money_flow: Direct instruments are public process infrastructure; signature/cost rules must not become pay-to-play.
modules.ownership: Ultimate political ownership remains with the people.
modules.household_effect: Citizens can correct institutional drift without elite permission.
modules.government_role: Rulemaker of process; Provider of neutral administration; Referee of rights floors on ballot measures.
modules.market_role: Petition/consulting industries compete under disclosure and anti-pay-to-play rules.
modules.transition: Preserve workable direct tools before inventing new institutions wholesale.
modules.risks: Ballot chaos; majority rights erosion; signature-industry capture.
modules.measurement: Access to tools; success/failure of citizen corrections; rights-floor compliance of measures.
modules.deferred_validation: Arkansas initiative redesign; People's Branch statute form — Stage 3/4

modules.name: Subsidiarity & Local Government
modules.now: Functions split across municipal, county, state, and federal levels with preemption, grant dependence, and uneven local capacity.
modules.problem: Wrong-level assignment creates remote capture or local incapacity; programs from Little Rock without local competence hollow places (joins HC-07).
modules.future_state: Clear assignment: which decisions belong with individuals, communities, municipalities, counties, Arkansas, or federal — and why — by subsidiarity and capacity.
modules.mechanism: Harvest federalism and community OS frameworks; regional shared services where county capacity fails; join HC-07 five-capital place capacity.
modules.money_flow: Each level owns distinct fiscal/operational duties; transfers should build local capacity, not permanent dependency.
modules.ownership: Local governments steward local public assets; state/federal hold enumerated shared roles.
modules.household_effect: Services at the nearest competent level without runaway remote bureaucracy.
modules.government_role: Rulemaker of assignment; Provider/Investor at the correct level; Referee of preemption abuse.
modules.market_role: Local enterprise embeds in place networks under layered regulation that does not double-capture.
modules.transition: Build local competence before centralizing more programs.
modules.risks: Home-rule theater; elite local capture; unfunded mandates.
modules.measurement: Function-by-level matrix clarity; dependency ratios; service quality by place.
modules.deferred_validation: Home-rule/preemption matrix; county regionalization list — known detail

modules.name: Competent Administrative Government
modules.now: Agencies, boards, commissions, and civil service deliver essential functions with uneven performance, opacity, and capture risk.
modules.problem: Administrative discretion is a primary capture surface; patronage and mission creep destroy competence and trust.
modules.future_state: Professional civil service, agencies, boards, commissions, rulemaking, service delivery, performance, and institutional accountability under continuous review.
modules.mechanism: Harvest government capacity / public service frameworks; performance and sunset review (LOCK-09); transparent rulemaking; civil service as capability not patronage.
modules.money_flow: Agency budgets are public capital stewardship; performance failure is leakage of household value.
modules.ownership: Agencies steward public trusts; they do not own policy or persons.
modules.household_effect: Reliable permits, benefits, safety, and services without arbitrary power or time-tax.
modules.government_role: Primarily Provider and Referee of process; Rulemaker via delegated rulemaking under statute; Investor/Owner only where justified and role-separated.
modules.market_role: Private contractors deliver under GO-06 rules; competition where appropriate; no sale of regulatory outcomes.
modules.transition: Improve highest-capture boards and delivery bottlenecks before wholesale agency redesign.
modules.risks: Capture of boards; sunset theater; under-resourced competence.
modules.measurement: Service timelines; complaint/appeal rates; sunset/performance review completion.
modules.deferred_validation: Highest-capture Arkansas boards inventory; sunset package — known detail

modules.name: Public Finance, Budgeting & Procurement
modules.now: Arkansas already budgets and procures at large scale; opacity and favoritism risk convert public spend into Capture Loop fuel.
modules.problem: Treating procurement as mere overhead misses that it is an economic-flow mechanism shaping ownership, competition, and capability.
modules.future_state: Public money budgeted, purchased, contracted, and invested transparently — supporting competition, Arkansas capability where lawful, and preventing favoritism/capture.
modules.mechanism: Bind Public Dollar Accountability Chain; open contracting; Money Engine join; ask of major purchases the five operating questions; guardrail against local-retention-as-favoritism; LOCK-06 ledger/replacement path remains bridge not COUNTABLE.
modules.money_flow: Revenue → budget → appropriation → procurement/program/investment → delivery → outcome. Leakage: favoritism, absentee extraction, captured incentives.
modules.ownership: Public money is community capital; vendors do not own the state; public equity stakes (if any) require role separation from Referee.
modules.household_effect: Better services per dollar; less extractive tax/service incidence as engines mature.
modules.government_role: Rulemaker of fiscal/procurement rules; Provider of budget transparency; Investor/Owner only under justified and separated roles; Referee against favoritism.
modules.market_role: Competitive vendors; Arkansas firms may compete without disguised patronage; price/quality remain live criteria.
modules.transition: Open contracting and measurement before aggressive preference schemes.
modules.risks: Commerce-clause conflict; favoritism theater; COUNTABLE inflation via procurement slogans.
modules.measurement: Open-contract coverage; competition metrics; retention vs concentration; outcome-per-dollar panels.
modules.evidence_status: WORKING — relationship bound; deep procurement research deferred
modules.deferred_validation: Commerce-safe Arkansas-capable procurement design; URT/school hard-core under replacement — Stage 4 / known detail

modules.name: Justice, Corrections & Public Safety
modules.now: Courts, policing, corrections, re-entry, fire, and EMS protect and also can extract via fees, incarceration traps, and weak accountability.
modules.problem: Coercive power without rights and restoration destroys household surplus and productive participation.
modules.future_state: Justice and public safety as rights-protecting institutions that preserve security and productive participation — including re-entry as human-capital recovery.
modules.mechanism: Harvest justice, equal standing, and constitutional defense frameworks; join HC capability and household surplus; treat private prison/extractive fee models as capture risks.
modules.money_flow: Public safety is core public duty; extractive fine/fee and private-corrections incentives are Capture Loop arrows.
modules.ownership: Facilities and supervision are public trusts; privatized coercion needs heightened conflict rules.
modules.household_effect: Personal security without asset-destroying justice traps; families retain productive members via re-entry.
modules.government_role: Referee of rights and law; Provider of safety/courts; Rulemaker of criminal/civil process — Investor/Owner of carceral assets under strict accountability.
modules.market_role: Vendors (medical, facilities) under GO-06; no market for selling justice outcomes.
modules.transition: Reduce extractive traps and re-entry failure before slogan-driven abolition/expansion fights.
modules.risks: Racialized enforcement; fiscal self-perpetuation; capture by private corrections.
modules.measurement: Safety outcomes; re-entry employment/ownership; fee burden; wrongful-harm remedies.
modules.deferred_validation: Corrections medical tension; diversion/re-entry package — known detail

modules.name: Anti-Corruption & Anti-Capture Architecture
modules.now: Campaign money, lobbying, conflicts, revolving doors, contracting, and patronage can purchase preferential rules.
modules.problem: Economic concentration reconcentrates political power — the Capture Loop antithesis of Constitutional Capitalism.
modules.future_state: Circuit breakers across Capture Loop arrows: transparency, competition, distributed political power, conflict rules, independent oversight, public measurement, citizen recourse, constitutional rights.
modules.mechanism: Establish eight breaker categories (not a 30-policy list); harvest LOCK-09 / transparency / forensic audit substance; join GO-02/GO-06; OpenFEC/OpenStates infrastructure as measurement substrate.
modules.money_flow: Stop converting public rules into private rents; disclose beneficial owners of influence and contracts.
modules.ownership: Politics fundable without donor ownership of policy; beneficial ownership transparency for influence and contractors.
modules.household_effect: Rules stay aligned with broad prosperity rather than donor portfolios; lower capture tax on prices and services.
modules.government_role: Rulemaker and Referee of anti-capture rules; Provider of disclosure systems; not captured Investor picking winners via pay-to-play.
modules.market_role: Competitive political and contracting markets under disclosure; no auction of policy.
modules.transition: Install disclosure and conflict breakers before maximal speech-adjacent redesigns that require Stage 4.
modules.risks: Free-speech doctrine conflict; under-enforcement; capture of oversight bodies.
modules.measurement: Disclosure completeness; conflict enforcement; contracting anomaly flags; trust/capture proxies.

modules.name: Data Rights, Privacy & AI Government
modules.now: Public data and AI tools expand state capacity; surveillance, automated decisions, and opaque models can silently become governing power.
modules.problem: AI assisting government can slide into AI becoming government without notice, explanation, or appeal.
modules.future_state: Public-data governance, privacy, surveillance limits, automated-decision rights, AI transparency, human appeal, and boundaries on algorithmic state power — rights-first.
modules.mechanism: Lock principle: AI may assist; must not silently become government. Consequential path: notice → explanation → human accountability → challenge → correction → auditability. Harvest LOCK-08 / systems-intelligence / transparency; legal standards Stage 4.
modules.money_flow: AI/cloud procurement under GO-06 anti-lock-in; public contribution to models may create proportional public claim (joins ME IP logic) without state owning all AI.
modules.ownership: Public data is a public asset with citizen rights; persons own privacy claims against unjust surveillance.
modules.household_effect: Service convenience without a control state; protection from automated injustice.
modules.government_role: Rulemaker of data/AI constraints; Provider of rights-preserving services; Referee of automated harm — not opaque algorithmic sovereign.
modules.market_role: Vendors compete on auditable systems; no proprietary black-box monopoly over consequential state decisions.
modules.transition: Inventory consequential automated decisions before broad AI deployment claims.
modules.risks: Surveillance creep; vendor lock-in; rights theater without audit capacity.
modules.measurement: Automated-decision inventory; appeal/correction rates; privacy incident rates; audit coverage.
modules.evidence_status: WORKING — principle locked; legal standards deferred
modules.deferred_validation: Privacy floor; public AI audit protocol; HYP-134 series — Stage 4 / known detail

modules.name: Measurement, Transparency & Public Accountability
modules.now: Build Progress, metrics, and transparency surfaces exist; continuous household/community outcome linkage remains incomplete.
modules.problem: Without continuous public measurement, government can claim success while household prosperity stagnates — capture hides in narrative.
modules.future_state: Arkansans continuously see what government promised, spent, produced, and whether household/community prosperity improved.
modules.mechanism: Harvest transparency / People's Ledger, baseline metrics, flourishing index, Build Progress; join Public Dollar Chain and HP surplus / HC pentagon outcomes; measuring stick itself must resist capture.
modules.money_flow: Measurement systems are public goods; open enough for citizen audit without violating GO-09 rights.
modules.ownership: Official statistics and dashboards are public trusts — not proprietary political assets.
modules.household_effect: Visible policy → household outcome link; trustworthy feedback into the Power Loop.
modules.government_role: Provider of open measurement; Rulemaker of reporting duties; Referee against cooked metrics.
modules.market_role: Independent analysts and media use open data; vendors of dashboards under open standards.
modules.transition: Publish spend/outcome joins on existing spines before new mega-dashboards.
modules.risks: Metric capture; privacy leakage; vanity KPIs.
modules.measurement: Publish rate of promise→spend→outcome chains; citizen auditability tests; surplus/place outcome panels.
modules.evidence_status: WORKING — remapped FIRST_PASS; deeper panels in 2.5/4
modules.deferred_validation: Geographic Money Statements; full Budget X-Ray — Pass 2.5 / Stage 4
